_comment: Every count this repository publishes about its own tree, with the measurement that produces it and every page statement of it (SPEC R306, INV-305). `scripts/gen-tree-counts.py` fills each generated block from the tree, and `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py` (gate ad) refuses a push where a published count and the tree disagree. An `argv` is a list of stages, each stage a list of literal argument tokens; it is run with no shell, through the program allowlist below, with patterns expanded inside the repository root, and the same list is what a reader is shown as the reproduction command. So this file is a CODE SURFACE: an edit to an argv changes what a push measures, and it is reviewed the way a change to a check script is reviewed. Sorting runs in byte order, so one command returns one order on every machine. A count states seven parts beside its number, and the generator refuses an entry leaving one of them empty: what it counts, its unit, the decision it informs, what changes when it moves, its baseline, its better direction, and its target. The eighth part is the method, and it needs no field: it is the published rendering of the argv. What no field holds and no gate reads: whether the count is worth publishing at all.

ground.decision: how much of the tree a push protects, and how long a push takes
ground.on_move: every push of this repository runs one more check and waits for it, or one fewer
ground.compared_to: the gate steps `.github/workflows/gates.yml` mirrors, which `guardrails/check-ci-mirror.sh` holds equal to this roster

better.reason: a roster that shrinks means a check was dropped and a roster that grows means every push waits longer, so neither direction is better on its own

target.reason: the roster holds to no number: a gate is added when a stated law earns one and dropped when its law goes, and a target would push against that

homes.template: **The gates are scripts.** {n} checks decide whether a push in your project is allowed.
The {n} are Python on the pre-push hook, mirrored in [CI](.github/workflows/gates.yml).
The {n} scaffold checks (completeness · tests-present · traces-to-spec · conflicts) run against the base diff

ground.counts: check scripts a host installs from `scaffold/guardrails/`
ground.decision: how much of a host project's push a gate covers once the host attaches this pack
ground.on_move: a host's push runs one more check, and three sentences on two pages state a number the tree no longer carries
ground.compared_to: the set `scaffold/guardrails/` ships, which is the whole set a host installs

better.reason: a check earns its place from a stated law, so a scaffold that grows without one is worse and a scaffold that drops a law's check is worse too

target.reason: the scaffold holds to no number of checks; it holds to one check per law a host project owes, and publishing a target number here would be the second typed count this entry exists to end
